answers: Police in Vermont say a car ended up almost vertical when the driver swerved quickly in response to her GPS ordering her to "turn around." The car was suspended almost vertically on guide wires attached to a utility pole (see a photo here) in Mendon on Wednesday night, reports the AP. Police say 30-year-old Nabila Altahan of Dorchester, Mass., was headed west on US Route 4 when she passed her intended destination and reacted quickly to the instructions, leaving the road at a significant enough speed to propel the vehicle up the wires. She wasn't injured. (This driver followed her GPS into a lake.)

full.prediction:
**Summary of News Passage:**

On Wednesday evening, a car was involved in an unusual incident in Mendon, New York, after its driver reacted too quickly to directions provided by a GPS system. The incident occurred around 8 p.m. near the Sugar & Spice Restaurant, on Route 4. Nabila Altahan, the driver of a Toyota Corolla, was following GPS instructions to turn around after passing her intended destination. Instead of gradually adjusting her course, Altahan reacted swiftly, causing the car to veer off the road and become suspended from a telephone pole's guy wire.

According to State Police, neither Altahan nor her passenger was injured in the incident. The car left the traffic lane while traveling westbound on Route 4, and the sudden GPS instruction led to the unexpected situation. A witness at a nearby miniature golf course reported seeing Altahan jump out of the car as it was suspended from the pole. 

Ray Ault, who was driving by the scene at the time, noted that both the State Police and the Rutland City Fire Department responded to the incident. The event highlights the potential risks of relying too heavily on GPS navigation systems, especially when drivers react impulsively to sudden changes in directions. While the situation was unusual and somewhat alarming, it appears to have been resolved without any serious injuries.
